origins: If conflict in our home meant screaming, silence for days, or violence, we learned to avoid it at all costs. Some churches also teach that disagreement is a lack of unity. The result is surface peace and hidden resentment, and relationships that cannot handle honesty.
teaches: Jesus taught, “If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.” Paul says, “Speaking the truth in love, we will in all things grow up into Christ.” Proverbs says, “Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed. The wounds of a friend are faithful,” and “the tongue of the wise brings healing.” Jesus said, “First go and be reconciled to your brother.” Handled well, conflict can strengthen relationships. Avoiding it can quietly erode them.
self_statements: If we disagree, it is over.
I must avoid conflict at all costs.
If I bring it up, it will explode.
errors: Imagining that any conflict will destroy the relationship.
Believing relationships are either conflict-free or broken.
Insisting that good relationships should have no tension.
questions: What did conflict look like in my family?
Have I seen a disagreement handled well? What made the difference?
What do I lose by avoiding hard conversations?
What would a calm, respectful way of raising an issue look like?
What does Scripture say about speaking the truth in love?
Is any conflict in my life unsafe, requiring outside help?
truth: Conflict handled with respect can strengthen relationships. I can speak the truth in love, listen, and work toward reconciliation. Where conflict is unsafe, I can seek help and protect myself.
hw_truths: The wounds of a friend are faithful.
I can speak the truth in love.
The tongue of the wise brings healing.
I can seek help if it is unsafe.
log: Each week, note one issue you raised respectfully and what happened.
actions: Begin with “I feel… when… I would like…”
Ask the other person to share their view.
If conflict involves threats or violence, call 911 or seek counseling.
prayer: Lord, conflict frightens me. Teach me to speak the truth in love, to listen well, and to seek reconciliation. Protect me where it is unsafe. Amen.
hw_questions: What did conflict look like at home?
What have I seen done well?
How can I raise an issue gently?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can speak the truth in love.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Conflict always ruins relationships.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
